author: The Linux Foundation
description:
It was an incredible three days in Minneapolis as the global open source community came together for Open Source Summit North America 2026, held May 18–20. This highlight reel captures the energy, collaboration, and innovation that defined this year’s gathering.

From keynotes and technical deep dives to hallway conversations and community celebrations, the summit showcased the people and projects shaping the future of open source.

What’s inside:
- Key moments from the main-stage and breakout sessions
- Insights from maintainers, contributors, and ecosystem leaders
- Demos and announcements from across the Linux Foundation community
- The spirit of collaboration that makes open source thrive

If you enjoyed this highlight video, share it with your team or community and keep the momentum going.

Explore more about the event through open source leadership or dive deeper into community building.
title: Open Source Summit North America 2026 Highlights & Key Takeaways (Minneapolis)

author: The Linux Foundation
description:
AI coding agents were built for flat files, not notebooks. Jupyter notebooks are JSON under the hood, which means line-by-line file edits break the interface, changes do not reflect in real time, and standard coding assistants cannot operate natively inside the notebook environment. The gap between how agents work and how data scientists actually work has been a real and unsolved technical problem.

In this exclusive interview with Swapnil Bhartiya at TFiR, Lahari Chowtorri, Technical Program Manager for AI/ML Open Source Strategy and Marketing at Amazon, walks through how Jupyter AI closes that gap, what is new in version 3.0, and where agentic notebook workflows are heading.

Key Topics Covered:
- Why existing coding agents fail with Jupyter notebooks and how notebook-native tooling and Jupyter Server Documents solve real-time sync
- How Jupyter AI 3.0 adopts Agent Client Protocol and Model Context Protocol to enable provider-agnostic, lightweight agent integration
- Support for ope
title: How Jupyter AI Brings Agentic Workflows Into Notebooks | Lahari Chowtorri, Amazon
